title: docs(adr): ADR-0162 closed states on an object close the record and its lines
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu2JFaDAE2Vf69revbwwFEXe)_

Part of #36253. This PR is the card's "ADR first" half. The build half stays on the card and starts only after this record is accepted.

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户无感：这次只落一份设计记录，线上行为不变；记录获批并实现后，业务人员会看到已付款、已审批通过这类已关闭的单据连同它的明细行，在任何入口都不能再手工修改或删除。
- 为什么做：属于「单据关闭后锁定」这项功能，替需要把已决单据冻结的应用解决问题，今天这些应用只能各自手写代码去拦。
- 出错会怎样：这份记录本身不影响任何人；其中的选择如果不合适，批准前直接改文字，批准后再出一份修订记录，没有数据需要回滚。
- 要你做什么：批准这份设计记录；你 11 月 26 日的三次裁定（「全部按推荐」、「平台堵住：撤回不恢复关闭值」和「平台拒绝这种配置」）已写进正文，正文里有三处你没有逐字说过：「已撤回」被设成关闭状态时撤回也不写它，比「不恢复」的字面更宽；已审批通过的单据被再次送审后撤回，会变回未审批，需要重新审批；「平台拒绝这种配置」在正文里写成发起审批时要满足的六个条件，比选项原话里的「缺少审批中状态或退回路径」更宽：审批的每一步都要写同一个状态字段，两步之间不能夹等待或表单，流程里不能在循环中逐条发起审批（比如逐行明细审批，要另起一个审批），状态字段不能带按条件只读或按条件显示的选项，以提交人身份运行的流程不能在两步之间改单据；拒绝发生在发起审批时，编写时会提前提示，发布时不拦。

## What changes

- Adds `docs/adr/0162-an-object-declares-its-closed-states-the-record-and-its-lines-are-closed-to-change.md`, status **Proposed**.
- Regenerates `docs/adr/README.md` with `scripts/adr-index.mjs` (one new row, three counts).
- No code, no schema key, no route, no changeset. The record declares; it implements nothing.

What the record decides, in the order the card asks:

| Card asks | Record answers |
|---|---|
| The key's shape | D1, D2: an object-level `closedStates` map from a state field to the values that close a record. Nothing is stored for it; closed is read off the stored row. |
| The unit | D3: the record and its direct `master_detail` lines, the unit the pending-approval lock holds. |
| Exemptions, and delete | D4 to D7: every caller is bound at every door, the state field included, and no grant lifts it. A write that names no principal is bound too. A system context is not bound. A caller cannot delete a closed record, and a delete whose cascade would reach one is refused whole before anything is removed. Referential clears, restore and a change of owner are named case by case. A new approval stays a way out of a state closed on the approval's status field, and an abandoned approval never writes a closed value. An approval opens on such a field only where the field can show it in progress, and the platform refuses the configuration otherwise (the third ruling, below). |
| One lock read | D8, D9: one refusal code, `RECORD_LOCKED`, with its own sentence. One read owned by the data layer answers for both producers, and tells every caller who can read the record whether it is locked and which lock holds. The approvals-family read stays exactly as published. |
| Where it is enforced | D10: in the engine's write path, after the object-permission and row-access gates and before the app's hooks. A many-row write is judged by one existence probe asked of the store. A line write asks the caller's own read door before it consults a master the write names. |

**Four points go past the ruling's words, and the maintainer has ruled on them.** The ruling of 2026-11-26 ([record](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/36253#issuecomment-7200732942), 「全部按推荐」, all as recommended) adopts each as the record writes it. Each stays marked in the text, with the other reading beside it in "Points the ruling does not settle":

1. D5: a system context is not bound at all, where the card's words require only a sanctioned action that moves the state. An action button's script is such a context, and works on a closed document as on an open one.
2. D6: a caller cannot delete a closed record, where a pending one can still be deleted.
3. D4: the lock is judged on the stored row only, so the write that closes a record lands whole. Item ③ of the 2026-11-22 batch governs `readonlyWhen` and not this lock.
4. D9: a new read owned by the data layer answers for both producers and names the reason. The approvals-family read stays as published and answers for approvals only; whether its routes retire or are redirected is a card filed with the build cards.

The same ruling settled three points the second contract review left open:

- **Who is told the lock's reason.** Every caller who can read the record. D9 states what that discloses to a reader whom field permissions keep from the state field, and why it is accepted.
- **A delete's cascade.** Judged whole, before the first row is removed. The refusal names the record the caller asked to delete and the label of the object in the way, and nothing of the closed record itself. D6 states the exception this makes.
- **A new approval of a closed document.** It stays a way out of a closed state. D5 names each outcome and where the author gates it.

**A second ruling the same day** ([record](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/36253#issuecomment-7201405662), 「平台堵住：撤回不恢复关闭值」, the platform blocks it: a recall does not restore a closed value) answers the point the third contract review raised. The new approval stays a way out, and D5 gains one platform rule. When a request is abandoned, by its submitter's recall, by an administrator's override or by the sweep of a dead run, the approval status mirror never writes a value the object declares closed, `recalled` included. The approvals-plugin change is a build card (Execution, item 7), released with the key.

**A third ruling the same day** ([record](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/36253#issuecomment-7205949718), 「平台拒绝这种配置」, the platform refuses this configuration) answers the point the seventh contract review raised. That review found that the record accepted, on its own word, a document left reading a decision, and closed, when its approval was abandoned before it finished. The seat put two answers to the maintainer, that the platform refuse the configuration that allows it or that authors be told how to avoid it, and the maintainer chose the first. The option reads 「字段声明了关闭值、却缺少"审批中"状态或退回路径时，发布或开审批时直接报错；作者补上选项才能用，单据不会假装已批准。」: where a field declares closed values and lacks an in-progress status or a way back, publishing or opening an approval fails with an error; the author adds the options before it can be used, and the document does not pretend to be approved. D5 carries the rule as the conditions on which an approval opens, and keeps the point marked ▲. An approval whose step mirrors onto a field the object closes on, at a status the mirror writes, opens only where six things hold: the field declares `pending` and the object closes on neither `pending` nor `returned`; a `state_machine` rule on the field lets a closed `approved` or `rejected` move to `pending`; the field carries no `readonlyWhen`, and its options for a request's statuses carry no `visibleWhen`; every approval step that can act on a record of the object mirrors onto that one field; no flow of the approval that runs as the user can write the record between two steps; and no flow of the approval pauses between two steps, on a node or on an approval of another record under a `map`. The whole approval is judged at its first request, from its definition. Otherwise that request is refused, with an error that says what is missing. D5 also states, all of it, what the refusal does not reach. **The six conditions go further than the option's words.** The option names an in-progress status and a way back, and an error at publish or at the opening of an approval. The record refuses when an approval opens and reports at authoring, and does not refuse at publish. Items 6 to 19 below are every choice inside the ruling that is the thread's or the seat's, and the header, D5 and "Points the ruling does not settle" say so.

## Small decisions

What earlier heads of this record called a round is called an approval from this head on, because ADR-0044 already numbers the rounds of a request.

The second ruling leaves the thread to say what the mirror writes in place of a closed value. Four choices are the thread's, and one, item 4, is the seat's reading. Each is stated in D5 and listed in "Points the ruling does not settle", with the ones not taken in Alternatives, "What an approval writes on a closing field, and where it may open":

1. **What is written instead.** The value a record that was never submitted carries: the field's declared default, or empty where the default is a closed value or there is none. The field does not go on reading `pending` with no request open.
2. **A closed value the approval did not write is left alone.** An approval is one passage of a record through its approval flow as a whole: the flow run started for it and every child run under it. Where the field holds a closed value that no request of the approval on that record had as its status, `pending`, `returned`, `approved` or `rejected`, the mirror writes nothing: another writer put the record there. Where such a request did have it, the mirror goes down the order. Where the mirror cannot tell, it goes down the order too: that costs a decision, and writing nothing could keep one that was never finished. The test reads what the field holds, and nothing from the value at submit, which a request does not always carry. The seat ruled the unit twice: the whole run after the sixth review, and the whole run tree after the seventh.
3. **Released with the key.** The key is not published while an abandoned approval can still write a closed value, or an approval can open on a field that cannot show it.
4. **A `recalled` the object closes on is not written either** (the seat's reading, by the text of the option the maintainer chose, on [record](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/36253#issuecomment-7202242844)). The field is then treated as one that declares no `recalled` value. The maintainer's own word is 恢复, restore, and the narrower reading, a rule on the put-back only, is in Alternatives.
5. **An empty value at submit on a required field is passed over.** The mirror goes on to the default, where today it puts the empty value back on every field. A required field that is not `readonly` refuses that write, and one that is `readonly` would be left empty. On a field that is not required the empty value is still put back.

Inside the third ruling, fourteen more choices are the thread's or the seat's, and none of them is in the ruling's words. They are listed in "Points the ruling does not settle", with the ways not taken in Alternatives:

6. **Refused when an approval opens, at its first request, and reported at authoring as early notice.** The objects and the flows are published apart, and the first request is the first point at which all of them are certainly in hand.
7. **An approval of one step is judged like one of several.** A single step fails too, on a decided document rejected into a status the field does not declare.
8. **`returned` is refused beside `pending`.** With both open, no failed write of the mirror leaves a lock behind.
9. **Of a `state_machine` rule one move is asked:** from a closed `approved` or `rejected` to `pending`.
10. **The conditions reach only an object that closes on a status the mirror writes** (the seat's ruling on the eighth review). An object that closes on its approval field only on values of its own, `paid` or `void`, is asked nothing, and its state machine may keep such a value final.
11. **The whole approval is judged at its first request, from its definition** (the same ruling): every approval step of the flow and of the flows it calls, each on its own mirror field and its own object, a `map`'s item object included. An approval that cannot be read whole is refused. The automation service hands every run its root run so that the plugin can do this, and Execution item 7 names that change.
12. **A mirror field carries no `readonlyWhen` at all.** The seat's ruling asks that none can hold on a closed value. The platform does not evaluate a predicate ahead, so the record asks that the field carry none. `readonly` keeps callers off it.
13. **A flow that runs as the user and can write the record between two steps is refused.** The seat's ruling left the record to choose between that and letting the approval's own run pass the lock. The record refuses the flow: a pass would exempt a caller's context from this lock, which D5 does for none.
14. **A run that ends between two steps is held to the same bound as a write of the mirror that does not land** (the seat's ruling): neither leaves a record closed on a value its own approval wrote and did not finish, and the key waits for the card that delivers both.
15. **Every approval step that can act on a record of the object mirrors onto the one field** (the seat's ruling on the ninth review, which asks it of a step that can follow one the conditions concern). Two readings inside it are the thread's. The first step of a new approval of a decided document follows the last decision, so the steps ahead of such a step are asked too. And a step in a `map` body counts as one that can act on the parent's record, because whether an item is a record is known only as the body runs.
16. **No option of the mirror field for a request's status carries a `visibleWhen`** (the same ruling). The check refuses it as it refuses a `readonlyWhen`.
17. **A pause between two steps is refused when the approval opens.** The seat's ruling left the record to choose between that and holding a run parked there to the bound of the status-mirror card. The record refuses the pause: it is in the flow's definition, and what can be read ahead is refused at the opening. A decision whose run cannot be resumed cannot be read ahead, and joins that card (the same ruling).
18. **A request the plugin cannot place as first or later is not judged** (the same ruling), so that no approval is refused between two steps. Only an approval whose run started before the key was released can be in that case.
19. **A `map` whose body holds an approval step is read both ways** (the seat's ruling on the tenth review): as a step of the parent's record, which names the field, and as a pause for it, because an item may be a record and the parent's run then waits on an approval of another record. It is refused unless the node shows that none of its items is a record. One collection can hold items of both kinds, so the refusal holds wherever the `map` stands among the steps. A node whose type publishes no descriptor counts as one that can pause (the same ruling).

One cost follows from the second ruling and is stated in Consequences: an approval of a decided document that is then abandoned leaves the document open, also when it was started by mistake, and it has to be approved again.

What the refusal does not reach is stated in D5, in "What it costs" and in "Points", and the record accepts none of it as a design. Three things cannot be read ahead: a rule or a hook of the app that refuses a write of the mirror, a run that ends between two steps because a node fails or the run is cancelled, and a decision that is recorded while its run cannot be resumed. For the three the record fixes what must hold: none leaves a record closed on a value its own approval wrote and did not finish, and a refused write of the mirror is no longer swallowed. It leaves the means to the status-mirror card, which Execution now names as item 8, and the key is not released before that card is built. A change to the object or to the flow after the approval opened is not judged again.

Five things follow for authors and are in Consequences. An object that already runs approvals meets the conditions before, or together with, its closed values: from the moment the declaration is published, a new approval is refused until they hold. An approval that keeps one status field for each stage, or leaves a stage without one, brings its steps onto one field, and a delay or a screen between two approval steps moves out from between them. An approval of each line, or of each of some other records, under a `map` is started as an approval of its own. An approval flow that runs as the user and writes the record between two steps is declared to run as system, or loses the write. And a refused opening reaches the person who submitted as a failed run.

**Read first**, by risk:

1. D5, "An approval opens on a closing field only where the field can show it in progress", "The approval is judged whole, once, at its first request", "What the conditions do not reach" and "An abandoned approval never writes a closed value", with their group in Alternatives considered.
2. D9, "Every reader of the record is told `locked`" and "What that discloses, and why it is accepted".
3. D6, "Cascades": what is judged, when, what the refusal names, and the exception.
4. D10, "A line write reaches a master in one of two ways", with the last group in Alternatives considered.
5. D5, the other outcomes of an approval, and which actions run elevated.

**Revised after the contract review of the first head** ([review](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/37606#issuecomment-7196241005), PASS with six points to fix and six nits). Every point is answered in the record's own text:

| Review point | Where it is answered |
|---|---|
| A many-row write should be probed in the store, not listed | D4, "Asked of the store, not listed" and "What cannot be judged is refused" |
| Item ③ was restated with a word the ruling does not carry | Header, D4's last paragraph, the third marked point, Alternatives |
| The showcase changes in more than two outcomes | Execution item 3, "What it costs" |
| `lockSource` has a published delete reading | D9: the delete reading holds only under an approval; the approvals-family read is left as published |
| Three kinds of writer, not two | D5, "The test" |
| The approval mirror moves a record out of a closed value | D5 and "What an author has to know" |
| The six nits | D8 (the upload-link door's own sentence; the refusal names no producer), D9 (two readability anchors), the Context table and D5 (the pending lock's other two passes), "What an author has to know" (create with lines), Readings (the unresolved case) |

**Revised after the delta review of `fe9a850c`** ([review](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/37606#issuecomment-7197474873), PASS with two points to fix and three nits) **and the ruling**:

| Review point | Where it is answered |
|---|---|
| D8 and D9 said the reason rule achieves more than the rest of D9 lets it | D9: the rule is gone; every reader is told the reason, and the disclosure is stated. D8 loses its sentence about the read. Alternatives keep both readings not taken. |
| D10's sentence was categorical, and the cascade was a case it did not cover | D10: the promise is scoped to the object-permission and row-access gates. D6: the cascade's judgement, its refusal and its exception. D8: the cascade's own sentence. |
| The per-row ceiling was misdescribed and misanchored | D4 and Readings |
| The upload-link door's sentence for a caller given no reason | D8: the door chooses its sentence by the read's reason, which a locked answer always carries |
| No alternative was recorded for the approval-round path | Alternatives, "A request is not opened on a closed record"; D5 |
| A line write and a master its writer cannot read | D10's two rules; D4, "One refusal is another gate's"; Alternatives |
| Where field permissions are asked | D10: in the security layer's middleware, ahead of the engine's hooks |
| What a change of owner does on a closed record | D7, "What an author has to know", the left-open list |

**Revised after the delta review of `f79eda94`** ([review](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/37606#issuecomment-7201298747), PASS with one point to fix and six nits) **and the second ruling**:

| Review point | Where it is answered |
|---|---|
| D5 and the author note said the state field always tells what happened | D5: each outcome is stated by the values the field declares, and the rule on an abandoned round follows. Consequences and Alternatives match. |
| The pending lock holds a pending round only where the approval node locks | D5, "While the request is pending" |
| Two writers that abandon a request were not named | D5, "Abandoned"; Readings |
| The cascade's sentence did not fit the second case D6 judges, nor say when it takes the label form | D8 |
| What a line's reader is told | D9, "What that discloses, and why it is accepted" |
| The ruling was quoted in English | Header: both rulings verbatim, with an English reading beside each |
| Three nits the review routes to the build cards: the `lockSource` member under an approval, a master that a hook supplies, an action's registered handler | Not changed here. They go to the build cards with the review record. |
| The ruling record's own wording | No change in this PR |

**Revised after the delta review of `eec0a5e1`** ([review](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/37606#issuecomment-7202211190), PASS with one point to fix and seven nits):

| Review point | Where it is answered |
|---|---|
| The "left alone" test stranded a record on an in-flight status the object closes on | D5 at that head: the mirror writes nothing only where the field still holds its value at submit (replaced in the next revision); a field the round left on a closed `pending` or `returned` goes down the order. The author's note, Execution item 7's test list and Alternatives name the case. D5 also states a case in which a record stays closed with no request open, on a required field with no usable default, and has the approvals card run it. |
| Two sentences on an abandoned round were true only of a round that opened the document | Consequences, both entries |
| A third thing inside the second ruling is the record's own, and "to the letter" was the wrong name for it | Header, D5, "Points the ruling does not settle", Alternatives: it is the seat's reading of the chosen option's text |
| The second ruling's time | Header: recorded at 19:16Z |
| "A stacked pair" in Execution item 1 | A trunk branch, as `AGENTS.md` has it |
| Three nits the review routes to the approvals card: the validator on a readonly field, the override arm admitting a system context, a log line when a value is withheld | Not changed here |

**Revised after the delta review of `32225e8b`** ([review](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/37606#issuecomment-7202670625), PASS with one point to fix and three nits):

| Review point | Where it is answered |
|---|---|
| The "left alone" test read a value at submit, which a request does not always carry | D5: the test reads what the field holds. At that head a closed value that is neither `pending` nor `returned` was left alone, and a field on either went down the order (widened to the run's own requests in the next revision). Execution item 7's test list gains a request that carries no value at submit. Alternatives records the earlier test as not chosen. |
| The case in which a record stays closed with no request open was stated in D5 only, and the record did not say it accepts it | D5 says the record accepts it, why, and what the case takes. The bullet heading above it, the author's note, "What it costs", two entries in Alternatives and the approvals guide of Execution item 7 carry it. D5's order also passes over an empty value at submit on a required field, so each way an author is given avoids the case. |
| Consequences said "opened" where the test is about the state | The author's note and "What it costs" speak of a round that moved the document's state, and say a decided document loses its decision also where it was never open during the round. |
| Any mirror write that fails is logged and swallowed, on every transition | Not changed here. It goes to the status-mirror card with the review record. |

**Revised after the delta review of `3c67c790`** ([review](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/37606#issuecomment-7203327629), PASS with one point to fix and two nits) **and the seat's choice between the two ways it offers**:

| Review point | Where it is answered |
|---|---|
| The "left alone" test was drawn against one request, and a flow run can hold several | D5: a closed value is left alone only where no request of the run had it as its status (the run became the whole round in the next revision). A closed value an earlier step of the same run wrote goes down the order, so a draft abandoned at a later step goes back to its draft value. The sentence on what the mirror has written speaks of the run. D5's accepted case (withdrawn in the next revision), the author's note, "What it costs", Alternatives and Readings carry it, and Execution item 7's test list gains a run abandoned at a later step after an earlier step was approved. |
| The step for an empty value at submit on a required field was not booked as the record's own choice | Header and "Points the ruling does not settle": one reading and three choices. Alternatives: the reading not taken. D5: the order is today's with two departures. D10's table says what changes for the mirror. |
| The test list lacked the arms that tell the chosen rules from their neighbours, and the step's reason held only for a field that is not `readonly` | Execution item 7's test list. D5 and the fourth reading under "Execution" state both kinds of field. |

**Revised after the delta review of `f7d2eb4c`** ([review](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/37606#issuecomment-7203817706), PASS with two points to fix and three nits) **and the seat's rulings on them**:

| Review point | Where it is answered |
|---|---|
| The "left alone" test was drawn against one flow run, and an approval can be spread over several | D5: a round is the record's whole approval, the run started for it and every child run under it. Each request records its round as it opens, the mirror asks its own table in one probe, and it goes down the order where it cannot tell. Execution item 7's tests and Readings carry the child run. |
| The record accepted, on its own word, a document left reading a decision its approval did not finish, and counted five conditions for one route out of several | D5 no longer accepts it. The question went to the maintainer, who ruled on it later the same day (the third ruling). On that head D5 was written to the seat's recommendation: the configuration is refused when a round opens. D5 says that the mirror's writes meet the object's validation rules, what an author who puts a `state_machine` rule on the field owes the mirror, and what the platform cannot read ahead. The paragraph of five conditions is gone. D10, Execution item 7, Points, Consequences and Alternatives follow. |
| The kinder alternative was turned down for the weaker of two reasons | Alternatives: that the two values are equal does not show the document stayed closed. |
| The test said "a status a request had", and the mirror never writes a closed `recalled` | D5 names the four statuses the mirror may have written. |
| The author's note said `approved` where D5 says "outcome", and gave the ways out as one pair | Those passages are replaced by the rule above. |

**Revised after the delta review of `4714072c`** ([review](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/37606#issuecomment-7204452910), PASS with three points to fix and four nits) **and the seat's rulings on them**, in two commits, `cbce67a5` and the head:

| Review point | Where it is answered |
|---|---|
| The check was made once an approval, while the mirror field is each step's own and the record each request's | D5, "The approval is judged whole, once, at its first request": every step of the flow and of the flows it calls, on its own field and its own object. The mirror's probe names the record. Execution item 7 says where the root run comes from, and its tests gain a first step with no mirror field, a `map` item on another record and a step two levels down. |
| What the refusal does not reach was wider than the one case stated, and its home was a clause | D5, "What the conditions do not reach", states the cases together. Two that the platform can read ahead are now refused when the approval opens: a `readonlyWhen` on the mirror field, and a write to the record between two steps by a flow that runs as the user. Execution item 8 is the status-mirror card: it takes a write of the mirror that does not land and a run that ends between two steps, and the key waits for it. "What it costs", "Points" and Alternatives follow. |
| The conditions reached further than their reason | D5: they concern an object that closes on a status the mirror writes, and the `state_machine` move is asked of a closed `approved` or `rejected` only. Booked in "Points", with the wider form in Alternatives. |
| "Round" already names something on a request | The record's unit is called an approval, and the word round is left to ADR-0044. |
| The status line and Provenance counted four marked points, all ruled | Five, four of them ruled on that head. The fifth was ruled later the same day. |
| "In two cases", and the two sides of a request the mirror cannot place | D5, "A closed value the approval did not write is left alone". |
